tools.description:
Poll an async enrichment job by task_id.

Pass the `task_id` returned by any async enrichment start tool:
sixtyfour_people_intelligence_start, sixtyfour_company_intelligence_start,
sixtyfour_people_bulk_intelligence_start, sixtyfour_company_bulk_intelligence_start,
sixtyfour_find_email_start, sixtyfour_find_phone_start,
sixtyfour_reverse_email_start, or sixtyfour_reverse_phone_start.

To cut the number of calls you make, pass `wait_seconds` (up to 25): the server
blocks until the job is terminal or the wait elapses, then returns. While status is
`running`, wait ~10s and call this tool again with the same task_id; only stop on a
terminal status (completed, failed, cancelled, terminated, timed_out). Do not answer
the user while the job is still running.
Completed responses include the upstream result and charge_credits inside `data`.
Bulk intelligence jobs return signed download URLs under `data.results`; non-bulk
enrichment jobs return inline data under `data.result` and usually include task_type.
To analyze a completed bulk job, read the numbered rows in data.result_page and
pass its next_cursor as cursor with the same task_id, or pass start_row to go
straight to a row. Page reads use saved data
and cost no credits. Supply page_size or columns to read the first page again.

```ts
mcp__Sixtyfour_Intelligence__sixtyfour_enrichment_job_status(args: {
// Return only these top-level result fields.
// default: null
columns?:
 | string[] // minItems: 1, maxItems: 100
 | null
,
// Opaque next_cursor from this job's result_page.
// default: null
cursor?:
 | string // minLength: 1, maxLength: 2048
 | null
,
// Read this many saved rows (default 10). Omit cursor and start_row to start at row 1.
// default: null
page_size?:
 | integer // minimum: 1, maximum: 100
 | null
,
// Start at this row number instead of a cursor, to go straight to a later row.
// default: null
start_row?:
 | integer // minimum: 1
 | null
,
// The task_id returned by an async enrichment start tool (intelligence or contact enrichment).
task_id: string,
// Optional. Seconds to block server-side waiting for the job to finish before returning (0 = return immediately, max 25). When set, the server polls internally and returns as soon as the job reaches a terminal state or the wait elapses — fewer round-trips for you. If it returns still running, call this tool again.
wait_seconds?: integer, // default: 0, minimum: 0, maximum: 25
}): Promise<{ data: object, ok: true, summary: string }>;
```

tools.description:
Start an async bulk People Intelligence job over many leads and return a task_id.

Do not return the task_id as your final answer — poll
sixtyfour_enrichment_job_status to completion first.

Use this to research the same custom `struct` for many people at once — e.g. the
leads you assembled from people searches. Provide the leads as either `rows`
(a list of dicts of known identifiers like name, company, title, linkedin) or
`csv_text` (a CSV string with a header row), but not both. The server builds the
upload file from your input.

`struct` is required. Each key becomes a field in the enriched output. Each value
can be a plain-English description or an object like
{"description": "Current job title", "type": "str"}.

To get phone numbers or emails, use sixtyfour_find_phone_start or
sixtyfour_find_email_start instead. They run the dedicated contact lookup; a
research job can come back without contact details they would find.

The start response includes estimated_cost_credits, a floor estimate.
Poll the returned task_id with sixtyfour_enrichment_job_status; the completed
response includes signed download URLs for the result files and the total
charge_credits. This is a billable job — if a start call times out, do not blindly
retry, since the job may already have been created.

Practical note: leads passed inline travel in the model's context, so this tool is
best for up to a few hundred rows assembled from searches. For larger user CSVs,
use the Sixtyfour web dashboard or call the bulk API directly.

```ts
mcp__Sixtyfour_Intelligence__sixtyfour_people_bulk_intelligence_start(args: {
// Optional subset of input columns to feed into the research agent. Defaults to all columns.
columns?: string[] | null, // default: null
// Raw CSV text including a header row, as an alternative to `rows`. Provide exactly one of `rows` or `csv_text`.
csv_text?: string | null, // default: null
// If true, return a confidence score for each requested output field.
field_confidence?: boolean | null, // default: null
// Optional methodology for where and how the agent should research.
research_plan?: string | null, // default: null
// Saved result file formats: "csv" (always produced) and/or "ndjson" (preserves typed values — numbers, booleans, nested objects). Defaults to CSV.
result_formats?: string[] | null, // default: null
// Rows to bulk-enrich, each a dict of known identifiers (e.g. name, company, linkedin, domain) assembled from search results or a file. Provide exactly one of `rows` or `csv_text`.
rows?: { [key: string]: any }[] | null, // default: null
// Also save JSON output artifacts alongside the CSV results.
save_json?: boolean, // default: false
// Required output fields to research. Each key becomes a structured_data field; each value is a plain-English description or {"description": "...", "type": "..."}.
struct: { [key: string]: any },
// Research depth and cost tier: micro (cheapest, returns up to ~5 fields), low, medium, or high. Omit to use the default (low).
tier?: ("micro" | "low" | "medium" | "high") | null, // default: null
// Optional HTTPS webhook URL that receives the completed results.
webhook_url?: string | null, // default: null
}): Promise<{ data: object, ok: true, summary: string }>;
```
